# Setting up CI

When initializing pre-commit in your repo with
`precommit::use_precommit()`, you can specify the continuous integration
provider with the `ci` argument:

- `ci = "lite"` (default) sets up
  [pre-commit.ci lite](https://github.com/apps/pre-commit-ci-lite), a
  GitHub Actions workflow leveraging the pre-commit ci lite action by the 
  creator of pre-commit.
- `ci = "native"` sets up [pre-commit.ci](https://pre-commit.ci), a
  fully managed service by the creator of pre-commit.
- `ci = "gha"` sets up a self-contained
  [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/features/actions) workflow relaying 
  on an action by the creator of pre-commit in maintenance mode.

For existing repos, use `precommit::use_ci()` directly.

Pre-commit runs hooks on all files in CI, so we recommend fixing all
problems locally before pushing by running roughly the same command as
CI does — see the next section.

# Emulate a CI run locally

In CI, a command roughly equivalent to the following runs from the
command line:

``` bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

If `pre-commit` is not on your `$PATH` (e.g. because you installed it
with `precommit::install_precommit()`), locate the executable from R:

``` r
precommit::path_pre_commit_exec()
#> "/usr/local/bin/pre-commit" 
```

Then run in your terminal:

``` bash
/usr/local/bin/pre-commit run --all-files
```

Fix any problems, stage the files, and re-run until the command
succeeds.

# Comparison

| Feature | `"lite"` | `"native"` | `"gha"` |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Auto-fixes PRs | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ [^1] |
| Runs on GitHub Actions | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| System dependency support | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Roxygenize hook support | ✅ | ⚠️ [^2] | ✅ |
| No workflow files in repo | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Periodic autoupdate PRs | ✅ [^3] | ✅ | ❌ |
| Requires GitHub App install | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Works outside GitHub | ❌ | 🔜 | ❌ |
| Workflow pinned to SHA | ✅ | n/a | ❌ |

[^1]: `"gha"` pushes fix commits but they do not trigger a new CI run
    without exposing credentials. You need to close and re-open the PR
    to re-trigger. `"lite"` solves this via the GitHub App.

[^2]: The roxygenize hook has limitations on pre-commit.ci: all package
    dependencies must be listed explicitly under
    `additional_dependencies`, there is a 120s build timeout, and system
    dependencies are not supported. See below for workarounds.

[^3]: Monthly autoupdate PRs require enabling *Allow GitHub Actions to
    create and approve pull requests* in *Settings → Actions → General →
    Workflow permissions*.

We recommend **`"lite"`** as the default. It combines auto-fixing (like
`"native"`) with GitHub Actions flexibility (like `"gha"`), and the
workflow files are SHA-pinned for supply-chain security.

## Notes on the roxygenize hook with `"native"`

[pre-commit.ci](https://pre-commit.ci) has three limitations relevant to
the roxygenize hook:

- {roxygen2} [requires loading your
  package](https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/issues/771), so all
  dependencies must be listed explicitly under `additional_dependencies`
  in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`. Generate the required snippet with
  `precommit::snippet_generate('additional-deps-roxygenize')`.
- There is a [120s timeout for building hook
  environments](https://github.com/pre-commit-ci/runner-image/issues/93#issuecomment-922505301),
  which may be exceeded for packages with many dependencies.
- System dependencies are not supported.

To work around these, you can:

- Disable the hook (comment out the relevant lines).
- Switch to `ci = "lite"` or `ci = "gha"`.
- Skip it on CI only:

``` yaml
ci:
    skip: [roxygenize]
```
